raw_comment:
Headline: Missing Water? Nationwide Droughts Occurring Throughout the U.S.

I notice that in in the Midwest, Central, and Middle-East that suffer a lot of droughts. Typically in the these areas do suffer the most droughts as they lack viable bodies of water especially in the middle of the U.S. The level of intensity varied among states however each state is currently facing some sort drought. 

I wonder why majority of the country is all facing some level of drought despite many areas having access to water. I wonder if these levels of droughts will continue to rise? Does the amount of droughts have a direct relationship to climate change and wildfires? How would this impact the availability of viable agricultural land? 

This relates to my community as drought conditions would drastically affect supplies of water, food, and the quality of air. For example while living in New York, with the recent Wildfires in New Jersey ended up spreading the smoke towards and around the area. Since the wildfire occurring in New Jersey was close to New York this led to the smoke being spread throughout New York as well.
